llm.summary: This is a legitimate web search skill, but it installs broad default-search behavior that can send ordinary user requests to an external service more often than users may expect.

dimensions.detail: Use of curl, jq, PRISMFY_API_KEY, and network calls to api.prismfy.io is proportionate for a search skill, but search queries and filters leave the local environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package discloses that it is automatically set as the default OpenClaw search tool and includes an agent bootstrap hook; no hidden installer or remote code retrieval was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill and bootstrap hook encourage natural-language and default use, including 'when in doubt' searching, which is broad enough to trigger external search without a clearly explicit user command.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The shell-profile API key setup is a disclosed user configuration step rather than a backdoor, but the installed bootstrap hook persists search-preference instructions across agent starts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bundled search helper, API key requirement, quota check, engine filters, and Prismfy API calls are coherent with the stated purpose of providing web search.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable making Prismfy the default search provider for the agent. Avoid entering secrets, private code, customer data, or confidential internal terms in requests that may trigger search, and consider narrowing usage to explicit /search-style commands if your environment has stricter privacy requirements.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill runs a bundled shell helper, which is expected for this implementation; the concern is downgraded because the script uses fixed curl/jq calls and no eval or remote payload execution was found.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending queries and filters to Prismfy is expected for a remote web search skill, but the privacy disclosure is not prominent enough given the broad default-search positioning.
[RA2] expected: The flagged shell-profile export is a disclosed way for the user to store an API key, not unauthorized session persistence.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad natural-language examples and bootstrap hook materially increase the chance that ordinary prompts are searched externally without explicit user intent.
[SQP-2] expected: The script transmits the query, selected engines, language, page, time range, and optional domain to the Prismfy API; this is purpose-aligned but should be clearer in runtime/help guidance.
